title: CultureVLM: Characterizing and Improving Cultural Understanding of Vision-Language Models for over 100 Countries
findings: The paper does not provide findings specifically for the 'Religion and Belief' category. The general findings indicate that Vision-Language Models exhibit significant regional disparities, with stronger performance on Western cultural concepts and weaker performance on African and Asian concepts. This suggests models would likely perform better on concepts related to religions more prevalent in the West (e.g., Christianity) than those from other regions, due to biases in the training data.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures a Vision-Language Model's ability to recognize, understand, and reason about visual representations of religious concepts. This includes identifying religious sites (e.g., temples, churches), ceremonies, and artifacts through multiple-choice questions covering image recognition, cultural knowledge, and scene reasoning.
